passage:
I'm Maria, and I still think about my cousin's farewell party. Somebody passed round a vape and a bottle, and the whole group looked at me. "Don't be boring, Maria," said one boy. My heart was thumping.
I laughed and said, "I'm good, my mum would smell it on me from two streets away," and took a plate of samosas instead. A couple of them groaned, but the moment passed. Simran, who had said no before me, nudged me and whispered, "Same."
We took the samosas out to the balcony and watched the street. Looking back, I had thought no would make me an outsider. It made me a girl with samosas and one real friend. Nobody mentioned it the next day.

qa.q: What did Maria take instead of the vape or bottle?
qa.a: She took a plate of samosas.

qa.q: What was Maria feeling when the group looked at her, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Her heart was thumping, so she felt nervous under pressure, and she had feared that saying no would make her an outsider.

qa.q: Why did Maria's joke and exit work?
qa.a: She said no lightly with a joke about her mum and moved to the balcony, which avoided an argument and let the moment pass. 😅

qa.q: How might Simran have seen Maria's refusal?
qa.a: Simran had already said no, so Maria's refusal probably felt like relief and company, which is why Simran whispered "Same".

grounding: Shows a teen offered cigarettes, vape or alcohol at a party and refusing with a joke and an exit.
